Trend analysis of a quantitative factor

Source: R/means.R
trend.Rd

Splits the sum of squares of a factor with numeric levels (doses, rates, dates) into linear, quadratic, cubic... components with orthogonal polynomial contrasts (also with unequal spacing) and fits the polynomial of the highest significant degree to the observations. A fitted quadratic reports where the maximum (or minimum) response lies.

Usage

trend(fit, factor, degree = NULL, alpha = 0.05)

Arguments

fit

An "ad_anova" object from design_anova().

factor

Treatment factor whose means are compared; two names compare all their combinations together (not available for split- or strip-plots, where by should be used).

degree

Highest degree to test (default: up to 4, at most the number of levels minus one).

alpha

Significance level.

Value

An object of class "ad_trend" with the table of components (components), the fitted coefficients (coef, intercept first), its R squared and the optimum of a quadratic (optimum).

Examples

fit <- design_anova(maize_nitrogen, "Yield_t_ha", "Nitrogen_kg_ha", block = "Block")
trend(fit, "Nitrogen_kg_ha")
#> 
#> Trend analysis of Yield_t_ha on Nitrogen_kg_ha (error: Residual error)
#> 
#>  component coefficients        ss         F df_error         p
#>     Linear -3, -1, 1, 3 19.770661 1203.4388        9 6.788e-11
#>  Quadratic 1, -1, -1, 1  1.775556  108.0780        9 2.587e-06
#>      Cubic -1, 3, -3, 1  0.004651    0.2831        9 6.075e-01
#> 
#> Highest significant component: quadratic.
#> Fitted response: y = 4.207 + 0.03323 x - 9.253e-05 x^2   R-squared = 0.946
#> Maximum response at x = 179.5 (y = 7.19); at the edge of the levels tested
